candidates.title: How Feedback-Free Self-Evolution Reshapes Agent Skills: A Systematic Study
candidates.citationVelocity: 發布 2 天，Semantic Scholar 回 404（尚未索引，同日 preprint 常見），引用數幾乎必為 0
candidates.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou) + HKUST + Knowin
communitySignals: 未見於 HF Daily Papers / Papers with Code（web_search 確認）；HF Daily Papers 完整清單本輪因輸出截斷無法核對排名
credibilityEvidence: Sec 2.1-2.2: 6 models (GPT-5.6-Luna, GPT-6.1-Sol, MiMo-V2.5-Pro, Claude Haiku 5.5, Qwen3.7-Plus, Qwen3.8-Flash) x 3 benchmarks (SkillsBench 87 tasks with deterministic per-container verifiers, LogicBench 760 Qs, MedCalc-Bench 1,100 Qs), 30 recursive feedback-free rewriting rounds per skill, every agent's pass rate falls below the original skill by round 30 (10.3-23.0pp across agents)
Sec 3.1: TF-IDF cosine-distance analysis shows rewrites move toward the model's own self-written-from-topic-alone priors across all models/benchmarks
Sec 3.2 Fig 3: item-retention tracking shows items outside the model's prior survive at 23.1% after 30 rounds vs 84.2% for items inside the prior

Sec 4 causal restoration experiment: putting back lost items outside the prior recovers most of the lost pass rate (about 2x the recovery from restoring other lost items), establishing causation not just correlation
Appendix B.7 swap test: both models perform worse with either model's round-30 rewrite, ruling out a model-specific artifact
SkillDiff method (marks prior-external content in place, no feedback, no rewrite) raises SkillsBench pass rate by 4.8pp average -- a working fix proposed and tested, not just a diagnosis
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: first systematic study of this exact failure mode, with causal (not just correlational) restoration experiments, a cross-model swap control, and a working mitigation tested on the same benchmarks; still single-paper, not yet externally replicated
reproducibilityEvidence: public GitHub repository with the rewriting pipeline and SkillDiff implementation; SkillsBench, LogicBench, MedCalc-Bench/SRA-Bench are public third-party benchmarks with deterministic verifiers
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: claim is narrow and precisely scoped to feedback-free rewriting specifically (not all self-evolution), and every number traces to a described experiment with a stated model/benchmark/round count
candidates.primaryLimitation: all three benchmarks (SkillsBench, LogicBench, MedCalc-Bench) pair tasks with pre-existing expert skills in a research-benchmark setting; whether real-world skill libraries (noisier, less curated) degrade the same way under feedback-free maintenance is untested
candidates.hiddenAssumption: TF-IDF cosine distance to the model's self-written-from-topic-alone skills is assumed to correctly identify which content lies 'outside the model's prior'; if a model's prior is better captured by embeddings or by what it would write with chain-of-thought rather than a flat topic prompt, some content classified as 'outside the prior' could actually be inside it
candidates.hiddenAssumptionImpact: the causal restoration experiment (Sec 4) directly tests the practical consequence of this classification -- restoring items classified as prior-external recovers far more pass rate than restoring other items -- so even if the TF-IDF proxy is imperfect, the behavioral evidence that *some* real distinction exists and matters would likely survive; the precise 23.1%/84.2% retention numbers could shift with a different prior-estimation method
candidates.presentationReason: explicit study design section, each of the two plausible prior hypotheses stated before testing, and an appendix section specifically designed to rule out alternative explanations (model-specific artifact)
candidates.reason: first systematic evidence that a real, already-widespread practice (agents rewriting their own skill files without feedback) actively destroys value rather than improving it, with a causal mechanism identified and a no-cost fix (SkillDiff) proposed and validated; frames the whole day's theme

candidates.title: Evolve Where It Matters: Coverage-Guided Self-Evolution of Agent Skills
candidates.citationVelocity: 發布 2 天，Semantic Scholar 429 rate limit 無法查得；preprint 剛發布，引用數幾乎必為 0
candidates.institution: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI) + University of Liverpool
communitySignals: 未見於 HF Daily Papers / Papers with Code（web_search 確認，僅見 arXiv 清單頁與自動摘要站 zerohour.day 轉載）
credibilityEvidence: Sec 5: 3 benchmarks (SkillsBench 87 tasks, SkillLearnBench 50 task families, SWE-Skills-Bench-Hard 70 tasks) x 3 executors (GPT-5.5/Codex, Opus 4.8/Claude Code, DeepSeek-V4-Pro/OpenHands), all deterministic verifiers (not LLM-judge pass/fail)

Sec 6.1 Table 2: leads both baselines (SkillRevise, CoEvoSkills) on every benchmark/executor combination; recovers 30/34, 32/38, 29/34 of SkillRevise's own recovered failures with the three executors respectively, showing gains are additive not just a reshuffle

Sec 6.2 ablation: removing the Coverage component (keeping the same RCA agent, same trajectories, same budget) drops recovery from 24 to 19 of 52 SkillsBench failures -- isolates the mechanism's contribution from general agentic trajectory analysis
Appendix G: explicit token-cost accounting showing SkillPlumber uses ~2x the tokens of baselines but spends them on producing the Coverage signal itself, not a hidden budget advantage
Explicit self-stated Limitations section naming the LLM-judge dependency of the Coverage labels and citing a separate validation against human labels for the same labeling task
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: three benchmarks spanning different task structures, three different executor/harness stacks, two real published baselines reproduced under a shared protocol, and a controlled ablation isolating the proposed mechanism
reproducibilityEvidence: SkillsBench, SkillLearnBench, SWE-Skills-Bench are public third-party benchmarks with deterministic verifiers; full prompts/protocol described in Appendices A-D; no public code repository for SkillPlumber itself found in the paper or via search this round
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: every headline number is tied to a stated benchmark/executor/baseline combination, and the paper openly reports where it does not lead (early rounds on one benchmark) rather than only its wins
candidates.primaryLimitation: the method's root-cause-analysis and coverage-labeling steps all depend on an LLM judge; the paper cites a separate validation study for the labeling task's reliability but does not re-validate it inside this paper
candidates.hiddenAssumption: instruction-level coverage labels (follow / not-follow / not-covered) are assumed reliable enough to drive revision decisions; the paper's own Limitations section names this explicitly and defers to a cited external validation rather than testing it here
candidates.hiddenAssumptionImpact: if the judge systematically mislabels a class of instructions (e.g. implicit ones not stated as discrete steps), SkillPlumber would misattribute some failures to 'wrong instruction' vs 'not followed', weakening the root-cause step specifically; the paper's own ablation already shows coverage matters more than generic trajectory analysis, so the overall performance gain is unlikely to vanish, but its causal attribution of *why* a given fix helped would be less trustworthy
candidates.presentationReason: explicit protocol section, ablation isolates the named mechanism, and a dedicated Limitations section flags the paper's own weakest link
candidates.reason: directly answers the question 2611.25534 raises -- self-evolution degrades skills *without* feedback, but this paper shows that properly scoped feedback (instruction-level coverage from real execution, not just outcome pass/fail) makes self-evolution outperform strong published baselines; the two papers together map both failure and fix for the same underlying problem

candidates.title: How Much Should an Agent Remember? Deployment Lessons from Self-Distilled Memory for LLM Agents
candidates.venue: Accepted to IAAI 2027 (Oral) -- peer-reviewed, accepted applications track
candidates.citationVelocity: 發布 2 天，Semantic Scholar 429 rate limit 無法查得；accepted paper 但剛掛上 arXiv，引用數幾乎必為 0
communitySignals: 未見於本輪 HF Daily Papers / Papers with Code 清單（但同一 altk-evolve 專案在 2026-04-08 已有 IBM Research 官方 HuggingFace blog post，確認是既有、非臨時掛名的production 系統）
credibilityEvidence: Measurement section + Insight 1 + Table 2: 8 models baselined (40-92% baseline task completion on AppWorld, a public third-party benchmark with authoritative pass/fail verdicts), 6 run with memory, dose-response curves across 0 to full guideline sets per model

Insight 5 explicitly measures the noise floor before reading any delta (identical configs scoring 56.0 vs 54.8 TGC; ~32/168 tasks flip outcome run-to-run) -- a self-imposed statistical discipline rare even in accepted venue papers

Insight 6: self-caught and corrected a baseline confound against a prior method (ACE) where a 'win' was mostly due to a different prompt scaffold, not the memory method itself; reports the corrected like-for-like comparison

Deployment section: re-ran results in two real IBM products (CUGA agent across 2 models/2 benchmarks with 3 trials each, reporting standard deviation-scale deltas honestly as 'below the noise floor' where applicable; watsonx Orchestrate production trace) after finding and fixing a silent write-path bug (Insight 7) that had made an earlier internal evaluation falsely show no effect
Explicit, numbered list of 7 'what went wrong' insights including a mislabeled page-limit guideline that caused a real regression, found and hand-fixed

altk-evolve is a pre-existing open-source library (confirmed via independent IBM Research HF blog post from 2026-04) integrated into shipping IBM products (CUGA, watsonx Orchestrate), not a one-off research artifact
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: combines controlled benchmark evaluation (AppWorld, with explicit noise-floor quantification) with real production deployment evidence (two shipping products); the production qualitative example is explicitly labelled 'descriptive rather than a controlled estimate', a self-disclosed boundary rather than an overclaim
reproducibilityEvidence: altk-evolve is a public open-source library (github.com/AgentToolkit/altk-evolve) with the described extraction/consolidation/delivery pipeline; AppWorld and tau-bench are public benchmarks with deterministic verifiers
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: the paper repeatedly narrows its own claims (e.g. downgrading a '+1.2 TGC win' to 'a tie at 1/7th the token cost' once noise and scaffold confounds are accounted for), which is exactly the discipline the selection standard rewards
candidates.primaryLimitation: the core acceptance mechanism for a guideline is recurrence (how many independent trajectories derived it), not correctness; the paper's own Insight 4 shows a popular-but-wrong guideline caused a real task regression that had to be fixed by hand, and the authors state they would not run the memory loop unattended without adding a correctness/recency signal first
candidates.hiddenAssumption: the paper assumes AppWorld's authoritative pass/fail verdicts and controlled train/dev/test split transfer to the production deployment case, where no such ground truth exists; the watsonx Orchestrate evidence is explicitly a single qualitative trace, not benchmarked
candidates.hiddenAssumptionImpact: the paper itself states this directly ('a single qualitative example rather than a benchmark') and does not claim the production numbers establish effect size -- so this is a disclosed scope limit rather than an unexamined premise the article needs to catch
candidates.presentationReason: the entire paper is structured around named, numbered 'Insight' sections that state what was expected, what happened, and what was changed -- an unusually explicit before/after format for a systems paper
candidates.reason: the only candidate today backed by a real, named production deployment (IBM CUGA + watsonx Orchestrate) and a peer-reviewed accepted venue (IAAI 2027 Oral), and its central finding -- that the right amount of self-generated memory depends on the model's own capability, not a universal setting -- generalizes the day's other two papers' point (self-maintained knowledge needs calibrated feedback, not blind accumulation or blind compression) to a different artifact (memory guidelines instead of skill documents) with production-scale evidence
